signal: LeagueApps acquired MOD11 and RecTimes in 2025 to expand its soccer and facility-management offerings, and partnered with Ankored on youth-sports safety compliance.

email.body1:
Grant, saw LeagueApps acquired MOD11 and RecTimes to expand soccer and facility management.

Rolling up new products that fast usually means more clubs and operators in play than the team can cover, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for LeagueApps off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Grant, quick follow-up for LeagueApps.

With the acquisitions widening the product line, the pipeline target probably grew faster than the team can. Most BD leaders cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings LeagueApps needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Grant, last bit of proof for LeagueApps.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how LeagueApps' reply rate likely compares to peer sports-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
